Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that is it from this game. The warm up games are done and we now move on to the main event. The ICC Women's World Cup kicks off on Tuesday, 30 September, with a thrilling opener between India Women versus Sri Lanka Women. The game will begin at 9.30 am GMT. Do join us for the early build-up and all the action as the tournament gets underway. Cheers!

Earlier in the game, Australia Women were restricted to 247 runs, thanks to Sarah Glenn's brilliant five-wicket haul. The Aussies had a solid start, with Litchfield (71) and Gardner building an 82-run partnership for the third wicket. Glenn's 16th over was a turning point, dismissing both Ashleigh Gardner and Phoebe Litchfield, triggering a collapse in the Australian middle order. England Women's spin attack, led by Glenn, bossed the first innings.

The English bowlers did the job today. Against a tough strong looking Australia Women team, they bowled really well. Sarah Glenn was introduced near the 16th over and spun a web around Australia Women as she ended with five wickets. Later in the chase, England Women lost three wickets inside the Powerplay but Alice Capsey and Sophia Dunkley's partnership seal the deal for them.

England Women comfortably win against their arch-rivals in the ICC Women's Warm-up match to boost their confidence much further. Australia Women will be gutted with how they have played. We saw a similar kind of performance in their recent tour against India where the middle order failed to capitalize on the good start which hampered their chances to post a threatening score. Today as well, Australia Women finish with 247 runs, which is a competititive total knowing they got bundled out with still 15 overs to play shows how important one partnership could be. Beth Mooney was the star with her fighting knock with the tail after Phoebe Litchfield's good start but they needed someone from the middle order to stay in the middle.
FOUR! England Women have done it. Shorter and on middle and leg. Alice Capsey pulls it to deep square leg for a boundary. England Women win by 4 wickets.
